intro.text: The biggest move was Heavy-AI Cash: money kept flowing into power semis, custom silicon, and physical AI hardware. AI Governance Board also heated up as firms wrote down risk and governance limits, while Power & Siting Crunch sharpened around electricity and data-centre locations.

threads.line: Heavy-AI Cash heated up as funding and industrial capex kept shifting toward power semiconductors, custom silicon, and physical AI hardware, from GaN plants to autonomous excavators and sensor chips.
AI Governance Board heated up as Anthropic formalized extreme-risk language in its S-1 and long-term governance plan, while other labs and researchers argued over trust, sourcing, and openness.
AI Trade stayed hot as capital rotated back toward tech and AI-linked assets, with broad tech gains and fresh funding for AI-finance and trading products.
Roll Tightening advanced as the Election Commission added a declaration to Form 6 and Karnataka’s final rolls showed a sharp drop after SIR deletions.
Refinery Shock heated up as Middle East attacks and Saudi tensions pushed crude higher and fed through to producer inflation in Malaysia.
Slow Math moved as turnout stayed high, exit polls delayed the verdict, and Arab-party gains pointed to a more fragmented coalition picture.
Power & Siting Crunch heated up as Anthropic said competition for electricity and data-centre sites is intense, while community backlash and cargo theft added more friction.

writer.watch: Watch whether the Heavy-AI Cash and Power & Siting Crunch threads keep converging: more chip fabs, power gear, and data-centre buildouts would confirm that AI expansion is increasingly limited by physical infrastructure. Also watch whether AI Governance Board turns into stricter filing language or real operational constraints.
